//: Argus Presenter — LOCAL DEPLOYMENT CONFIG (Plan 0522 P16.1/P16.2). Copy to presenter-config.json (gitignored) or to ~/.config/argus-presenter/presenter-config.json, then edit. NO FILE IS REQUIRED: with none of them present the presenter runs on port 3000 and logs sessions to ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/argus-presenter/logs.
//resolution: First file found wins, WHOLE FILE — not key-by-key: $PRESENTER_CONFIG_FILE (must exist) > <repo>/presenter-config.json > ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/argus-presenter/presenter-config.json > built-in defaults. Loader: lib/deployment-config.mjs.
//resolution-trap: BECAUSE IT IS WHOLE-FILE: a repo-local presenter-config.json that sets ONLY presenterPort makes an ~/.config file containing sessionLogDir INVISIBLE — the second file is never opened, and the log falls back to the built-in default. Keep every key you care about in the SAME file. GET /api/session-log reports sessionLogDirSource ('env' | 'config' | 'built-in'), so you can see which one actually won.
//presenterPort: The port the presenter binds — used by `node app/server.mjs` with no argument AND by the presenter_start MCP tool. It must match whatever your public ingress (tunnel/reverse proxy) forwards to, or the session is unreachable while every local check says 200. 0 = let the OS assign one.
//sessionLogDir: Plan 0522 P16.2 — where the DURABLE SESSION LOG goes: one JSONL file per session, one line per durable op, so a session's record outlives the process that made it (the in-memory op-log is a 1000-entry ring and is freed at exit). MUST BE OUTSIDE ANY REPOSITORY — a path inside the checkout is REFUSED and the log disables itself, because these lines carry the session transcript. Omit the key to get ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/argus-presenter/logs; $PRESENTER_SESSION_LOG_DIR overrides both. Reading it over HTTP (GET /api/session-log) requires the control credential and FAILS CLOSED when none is configured, so set rolePassword or controlToken if you want to read it. Caps: 4 MiB per part, 4 parts per session, 50 sessions retained, oldest dropped.
//enforceOAuth: Plan 0543 — the AUTH POLICY dial. Governs the CONTROL PAGE (drive-the-presentation) ONLY; it NEVER governs command-trust (whose words may become an instruction to Argus). Command-trust is ALWAYS identity-gated: a true-loopback connection, or a verified+allowlisted OIDC/tailscale principal. A shared password NEVER commands Argus. Values: 'off' (default) — the tissue-thin password OR a verified identity may open the Control page; 'control' — the Control page requires a verified+allowlisted principal (password retired for control) AND a break-glass credential must be configured or the server refuses to start. An unknown value is a startup error, never a silent default.
//allowPasswordCommandOnLAN: Plan 0543 — an explicitly-unsafe escape hatch (default false). When true, a password-holder MAY command Argus, but ONLY from a non-loopback PRIVATE-LAN address with NO forwarding header — never over the tunnel. Leave false unless a deployer knowingly wants a trusted-LAN shared-secret command path.
//rooms: Plan 0674/0675/0684 — A ROOM IS A CONTEXT, AND ITS CAPABILITIES ARE CONFIG. One OS process serves one room; `$PRESENTER_ROOM` names which key of this map that process serves, and an unset variable means `defaultRoom`. ⛔ A `$PRESENTER_ROOM` naming a room that is not declared here is a NAMED STARTUP ERROR, never a fall-through to defaultRoom: a process booting with somebody else's capabilities looks healthy, answers, and quietly serves a policy nobody chose. ⛔ EVERY CAPABILITY IS FAIL-CLOSED WHEN ABSENT — plugins [], record "none", voice false, profile null, pluginsDir null. Absent NEVER means inherit. ⚠ Keys this loader does not know about ride through untouched, so a later version's capability written here today is not destroyed by today's code.
//rooms-keys: port (1..65535; 0 refused — a room's port is an address other things must name) · bindHosts (same rules as the deployment-wide key; a wildcard is refused) · plugins (an ARRAY of names; a bare string throws, because iterated it is a list of its own characters) · record ("none" or a retention duration like "30d"; the BOOLEAN true throws) · voice (the JSON boolean; the STRING "true" throws) · profile (the behaviour-profile name) · pluginsDir (where this room's plugins are read from) · label (human-facing only).
//rooms-transcriptDir: Plan 0684 R2 — ⛔ A ROOM THAT RECORDS MUST NAME transcriptDir, and it is a NAMED STARTUP ERROR if it does not (either here, or via $PRESENTER_TRANSCRIPT_DIR). It must be an ABSOLUTE path OUTSIDE the release tree. WHY: the in-code fallback resolves to <release>/.transcripts, the deploy pipeline keeps ten releases and prunes the rest, so recording without setting it WORKS — visibly, at every moment you might check — and is then deleted by a later prune. There is no point at which it looks broken. ⚠ pluginsDir is deliberately NOT under this rule: plugins are code and ship inside the release.
//rooms-mcpPort: Plan 0684 R5 — THE MCP CONTROL PORT IS A PROPERTY OF THE ROOM. $PRESENTER_MCP_HTTP is process-global, so two room processes started from one unit template both try to bind it: the second dies at a moment nothing is watching, or the tools attach to whichever won and an operator drives the wrong room believing they are driving this one. ⛔ TWO ROOMS DECLARING THE SAME mcpPort IS A NAMED STARTUP ERROR, never last-writer-wins — and so is a room whose mcpPort is its own http port. The env fallback keeps $PRESENTER_MCP_HTTP's existing meaning (0 or unset = no HTTP MCP), but a value that is not a port number now throws instead of coercing to NaN and quietly never binding.
//rooms-env-fallback: Plan 0684 R1 (guard G13) — CONFIG BEATS ENV BEATS THE FAIL-CLOSED DEFAULT, and the startup line reports which of the three each value came from. The environment variables remain as DOCUMENTED FALLBACKS, not as the source of truth: profile ← $PRESENTER_PROFILE, voice ← $PRESENTER_VOICE_ENABLED, pluginsDir ← $PRESENTER_PLUGINS_DIR. ⛔ An unrecognised boolean token in $PRESENTER_VOICE_ENABLED is a NAMED STARTUP ERROR, not "off": accepted are 1/true/on/yes/y/enabled and 0/false/off/no/n/disabled. ⛔ `record` has NO environment fallback on purpose — it is a RETENTION POLICY, not a switch, and a duration nobody wrote down is how a transcript outlives the consent that permitted it.
//identity: Plan 0551 P1 — IDENTITY (oidc / allowlist / tailscale / breakGlass / revokedNonceFile) IS READ FROM THIS FILE, by BOTH launch paths (`node app/server.mjs` and the presenter_start MCP tool). It is deliberately NOT on presenter_start's input schema: an agent that could name its own allowlist could authorize itself. ⛔ EVERY KEY BELOW IS COMMENTED-OUT ON PURPOSE — the examples are `//`-prefixed doc strings, never live keys. A real client id or secret must NEVER appear in this file: presenter-config.example.json is TRACKED IN GIT. Put real values in presenter-config.json (gitignored) and type the secret yourself.
//identity-trap: ⚠ Resolution is WHOLE-FILE, first found wins (see //resolution above). Adding the oidc block to a DIFFERENT file than the one already winning makes it INVISIBLE: OIDC boots inactive, /auth/login answers 404, and the page shows no sign-in control. Keep identity in the SAME file as presenterPort. The startup line says which file won and whether OIDC came up — read it.
//oidc: The OAuth 2.0 / OIDC client. ABSENT ⇒ sign-in is off, /auth/login is a clean 404, and the clients show no sign-in control. PRESENT-BUT-INCOMPLETE ⇒ the server REFUSES TO START with a named IdentityConfigError, because a half-configured block means the deployment intended sign-in and booting it silently off is the exact bug Plan 0551 exists to kill. ALL of clientId, clientSecret, authEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, redirectUri, issuer, jwksUri are required. `issuer` is required because verifyIdToken SKIPS the `iss` check when it is absent; `jwksUri` is required because defaultOidcDeps().fetchJwks reads it, and without it a successful Google sign-in fails at the callback. Optional: `scope` (default "openid email profile").
//oidc-example: "oidc": { "clientId": "REPLACE-ME.apps.googleusercontent.com", "clientSecret": "REPLACE-ME — type it yourself; never paste it into a transcript", "authEndpoint": "https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth", "tokenEndpoint": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token", "jwksUri": "https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs", "issuer": "https://accounts.google.com", "redirectUri": "https://YOUR-PUBLIC-HOST/auth/callback" }
//oidc-redirect: redirectUri must match the IdP's registered redirect EXACTLY — scheme, host and path. It is the PUBLIC url participants reach (the tunnel/ingress address), never 127.0.0.1, because that is the origin the browser is on when it comes back.
//allowlist: FAIL-CLOSED authorization: the map from a verified principal's email (OIDC) or tailnet user (tailscale) to a role. Being signed in is NOT being authorized — a verified principal that is not on this list authenticates and still arrives `participant`, FENCED. ABSENT or {} authorizes NOBODY. Keys are trimmed + lowercased. Value is {"role":"presenter"} or the shorthand "presenter". This list is the only thing between a Google account and command authority over Argus; keep it short.
//allowlist-voice: OPTIONAL per-entry capability: {"role":"presenter","voice":true} grants the MICROPHONE to that principal. ABSENT ⇒ false (fail-closed): being allowlisted as presenter does NOT by itself grant voice. MUST be the JSON boolean true — the string "true" is a startup error, deliberately, because a capability that silently reads as false costs a debugging session to find.
//tailscale: Enables the DIRECT-tailnet-peer identity adapter: {"enabled": true}. ⚠ Inert unless the server is reachable at its tailnet address — it binds 127.0.0.1 today, and over a tunnel the peer is the tunnel daemon, never the phone. Leave absent unless the bind has been changed deliberately.
//breakGlass: The local recovery credential whose PRESENCE is the startup gate for enforceOAuth:"control" (an IdP outage would otherwise lock everyone out). Shape: {"token":"…"} or {"file":"/path/to/break-glass"} (0489 §4.6: loopback-only, single-use, TTL, mode 0600). Required only when enforceOAuth is "control".
//revokedNonceFile: Where revoked guest-link (cap) nonces are persisted so a revocation survives a restart. Absent ⇒ both launch paths derive `revoked-caps.json` inside the resolved session-log/state directory, which is what you want. Set it only to move that file deliberately.
